classification.habit: Annual herb or small branched herb
classification.habitat: Open fields, roadsides, wastelands and disturbed ground, especially during the rainy season
classification.distribution: Widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions including India; local occurrence should be confirmed in field work

identification.description: A characteristic Senna herb with paripinnate leaves, paired leaflets and yellow flowers; mature pods and seed characters are useful for confirmation.
identification.whole_plant: Erect, branched annual herb, usually arising in disturbed/open ground.
identification.root: Slender primary root with lateral roots; detailed pharmacognostic characters require authenticated specimen study.
identification.stem: Green to reddish-brown, branched, generally cylindrical and becoming firmer with age.
identification.leaf: Paripinnate compound leaves with several pairs of opposite leaflets; a small gland may occur on the rachis near the lower leaflet pairs.
identification.flower: Yellow, typically five-petalled flowers borne in the leaf axils or short clusters.
identification.fruit: Long, slender, somewhat curved to sickle-shaped pod containing multiple seeds.
identification.seed: Numerous hard, flattened, angular to rhomboid seeds, brownish to dark in mature pods.
identification.bark: No separate bark character should be used for routine authentication of this annual herb.
identification_points: Differentiate from other Cassia/Senna species by botanical characters

modern_information.safety_notes: Avoid self-prescribing concentrated preparations or purgative doses. Correct species identification and authoritative formulation guidance are important.
